messages.author: b277f4bfe1bf5a8d
messages.subject: Potentially Missing Warning Messages
parts:
Hello lavaan community,

I am running a SEM analysis with 20 multiply imputed data sets in lavaan 0.6-9. The model converged on 14 data sets. For the remaining 6, standard errors could not be computed. I am running the model on those six individual data sets, and I am getting a message that there are 21 warnings. However, when I use "warnings()" to view them, only one is displayed: "In .local(object, ...): lavaan WARNING: fit measures not available if model did not converge."

I'm not sure if this output means that there is only 1 warning that was repeated 21 times, or if there are 20 additional warnings that are not displaying for some reason. Would anyone happen to know if it is just one warning or if it is missing warnings? Also, if there are 20 warnings that are not displaying, does anyone know how to figure out what they are?

Thanks,

Ryan

messages.subject: Re: Potentially Missing Warning Messages
parts: Thanks, and that is indeed quite a model.   How many variables, and thresholds per ordered variable?  As large as your sample seems, consider how many summary statistics you are trying to reproduce.  A low N-per-statistic is associated with problems estimating the asymptotic covariance matrix of model parameters, from which standard errors are derived (also the weight matrix is derived from the asymptotic covariance matrix of the estimated polychorics/thresholds, so the same issue can manifest in different stages of DWLS estimation).

I am getting a message that there are 21 warnings. However, when I use "warnings()" to view them, only one is displayed: "In .local(object, ...): lavaan WARNING: fit measures not available if model did not converge."

Perhaps what is happening is that the 21 warnings are accumulated during the sem() call, but then another warning is returned by summary() that clears the previous cache of warnings().  Perhaps you could verify this by calling warnings() immediately after sem().

If this doesn't resolve the issue, you could set options(warn = 1) to print warnings as they occur, then set it back to the default options(warn = 0) after.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
